text:
tasha: Helios follow-up: hosted POC with browser SSE + server workers. Needs function/tool calling, strict JSON schema output, SAML SSO, and customer-managed KMS (BYOK). They want a cost estimate for short bursts (~1k qps for 15-30m).

vik: Quick q: demo creds ephemeral in browser? and will they consent to a small legal LOA for BYOK?

tasha: Yes ephemeral creds preferred. They can sign LOA for KMS but want timeline. Also SOC2 evidence requested.

rachel: Tech notes: Node/Python SDKs support streaming and function calls. Browser best-effort via SSE; server agents should use websockets for lower overhead. Function calls surface as stream events (type: "function_call") with args as JSON. For strict structured output we recommend embedding a JSON Schema in system instructions and validating the assembled object client-side once stream completes.

vik: One caveat: current client behavior with short-lived tokens + SSE can cause reconnect storms if token rotates mid-stream. Workarounds: proxy token refresh on server or reconnect with replay. We're finalizing an auto-refresh fix in PR #1366.

security-bot: BYOK on hosted requires enterprise plan + KMS verification and LOA. SOC2 artifacts can be shared under NDA. If they need custom audit retention, that's an add-on. Expect legal lead time ~2-3 weeks.

tasha: Latency question: can we hit ~100ms p50 for small prompts?

rachel: Hosted is best-effort. Dedicated/reserved capacity + quantized model + batch=1 can reach ~100ms p50. Recommend pinned model + prefix caching for demo.

vik: I'll draft a one-page runbook: SSE example, websocket fallback, function_call handling, schema validation pattern, token-rotation workaround, and a simple cost calc for the burst scenario. Will include short quickstart repo link.

ci-bot: PR #1366 opened by @vik - "sse-token-auto-refresh" (CI checks queued).

tasha: Thanks — I'll share Helios contact (emma@helios.com) and schedule a Wed demo. Tagging @rachel @vik for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
